title: Best UX Designers (2026): How to Hire One for Your Product
description: How to hire a UX designer: what the project should include, how to brief it, what drives the price and the red flags to avoid.
intro: UX design is about how a website or app works for the people using it: what they need, where they get stuck and how they reach their goal. Good UX saves development time because problems are found in a prototype, not in code. Projects disappoint when the work stays at pretty screens without research or testing. This guide helps you ask for the real thing.

faq.q: What is the difference between UX and UI design?
faq.a: UX design covers structure and flow: what screens exist, what is on them and how users move between them. UI design covers the visual layer: colors, type, buttons and polish. Many designers do both, but check which the package covers.

Wireframes are simple layouts of each screen, without final visuals. A prototype links screens so you can click through the flow as if it were real. Both let you test ideas before paying for development.
Some research almost always helps, even a few short interviews or tests with real users. It shows problems you cannot see yourself. Ask what research is included and how findings will be shared.

faq.q: Which tool will the designer use?
faq.a: Figma is the most common. Ask for access to the file, not just images, so your developers can inspect sizes and export assets.

faq.q: Can a UX designer improve an existing product?
faq.a: Yes. A UX audit reviews your current site or app, finds problems and suggests fixes. It is often a good first project before a full redesign.
